action: Move staff and IT-supplier accounts to phishing-resistant MFA, and stop relying on SMS or voice codes for sign-in and account recovery, since SIM swaps let attackers intercept them.
exec: SMS phishing of staff and contractors plus SIM swaps drove company breaches and crypto theft; phishing-resistant MFA limits both routes.
impact: At least a dozen companies breached; at least $11.6 million in virtual currency stolen from individuals across the US.
org: US Attorney's Office, Central District of California
plain: A Scottish man was jailed for six years in the US for sending fake work texts to staff at a dozen companies, breaking into their systems and hijacking people's phone numbers to steal $11.6 million in crypto.

report.publisher: US Attorney's Office, Central District of California
key_findings: Buchanan was sentenced to 72 months by US District Judge John W. Holcomb; a restitution hearing is set for 11 December.
He pleaded guilty on 17 April to conspiracy to commit wire fraud and aggravated identity theft and has been in custody since April 2025.
Victims included entertainment, telecoms, technology, BPO and IT suppliers, cloud communications and virtual currency firms.
A phishing kit sent captured credentials to a Telegram channel run by Buchanan and a co-conspirator; SIM swaps were used to bypass two-factor codes.
Four co-defendants were sentenced to terms from two to ten years.
recommendations: The release gives no guidance for organisations or the public.

sources.name: US Attorney's Office, Central District of California (DOJ release 26-220)

summary: Tyler Robert Buchanan, 24, of Dundee, Scotland, was sentenced in Santa Ana to 72 months in federal prison. From September 2021 to April 2023 he and co-conspirators sent SMS phishing messages to employees of at least a dozen companies, used the stolen credentials to break in, and SIM-swapped individuals to steal at least $11.6 million in virtual currency. He is the fifth and final defendant sentenced.
title: DOJ: British man gets six years for SMS phishing intrusions and $11.6M virtual currency theft
